# Creature filters

- The asset manager's Characters tab filters tokens by their linked statblocks (`src/app/creatures/`). Only tokens are listed; a statblock without a token never is.
- Filters come from the statblocks, not the game system: `CATALOG_CREATURE_FILTERS` (`creatureFieldCatalog.ts`) names the fields Fantasy Statblocks layouts share (Challenge rating `cr`, Level, Tier, Type, Traits, Rarity, Alignment, Source), and the sidebar shows each only where the statblocks in view have its field. A collection may switch catalog filters off (`CollectionSettings.hiddenCreatureFilters`, by id) and add filters on other fields (`customCreatureFilters`); read both with `collectionCreatureFilters`. Never change a catalog id. A range filter reads exactly one field so scales never mix; an options filter may merge several (Pathfinder's `trait_01`…).
- `CreatureIndex` (one per app, released in `onunload`) resolves note paths through `resolveLinkedCreature`: the bestiary entry, else the note's frontmatter (Fantasy Statblocks parses notes only with "auto parse" on), else its statblock fence. It re-reads a note on metadata change and all notes once the bestiary settles after an update, and keeps old entries readable meanwhile. React reads it with `useCreatureIndex` (`useSyncExternalStore`). Fantasy Statblocks parses the vault after every start, and until that is done (`isBestiaryResolved()` false) its `getCreatureFromBestiary` throws: read a creature by name only through `bestiaryCreatureByName` (`FantasyStatblocksService.ts`), which has none until then. `hasCreatureForNotePath` can be asked during the parse, but a note the parse has not reached is not held until it has. During the parse a null from `resolveLinkedCreature` means "not known yet", and a creature that `extends` another comes without it. `FantasyStatblock` shows the bestiary's entry for the note's path, else what `resolveLinkedCreature` reads (the note's own statblock before the bestiary creature of its name), so a statblock waits for the parse only where it needs a bestiary creature by name, and then as a skeleton. A link made during the parse writes the statblock into the map files only where it is known whole (a creature that is there and extends nothing); otherwise the files get the link alone (`statblockPath`), and nothing is written later, so those tokens keep their name and difficulty until they are linked again (`TokenStatblockLinkService.extractStatblockData`, `wholeOnly`). Token placement (`loadStatblockOverrides`) and `fillMissingResources` read during the parse too and store what they find: it can lack what only the bestiary has, and is never wrong. **Statblock values** (`creatures/statblockValues.ts`): a statblock is a note's text, not Atlas' own data, so it is read within `STATBLOCK_LIMITS` (depth, entries of a list or map, length of one text, values and characters of the whole statblock; one budget per statblock). `resolveLinkedCreature` and `resolveCreatureFromFence` return a bounded copy named by a text (`namedStatblock`); token placement, the link written into map files, `fillMissingResources`, senses and the filters (`CreatureIndex`) read that. `FantasyStatblock` takes a bestiary entry or a note's text directly, so it bounds the statblock it hands to the renderer, the token rows and the dice (`boundedStatblock`), and `StatblockRenderer` bounds its own prop. Two kinds of reader take a statblock as it came: those that read single fields by key and check their type (`resolveField`, through which an open map reads a note's frontmatter for its tokens' resources, `label`, `layoutForCreature`, the importer's `statblockImportCandidate`), and the link dialog's list of the bestiary's own entries (`statblockEntries`, which names each through `valueText`). Anything else that takes a creature from the bestiary (`bestiaryLookup`, `getBestiaryCreatures`) or a note's frontmatter bounds it before it walks it. `valueText` writes a value as text within the limits (the renderer's `stringify` and the trait reader are it); `parseOptions`, `sensesTextOf` and `frontmatterLabel` make text too and rely on being given the copy. `StatblockMarkdown` and `sensesTextOf` join texts and cut the result again with `boundedText`. A block takes no value's type for granted: a name, a description or a list entry may be a number, a list, a map or nothing, and a traits block skips only an empty entry, since a layout's callback may draw a word or a pair. The YAML of a note, a base or a bundle is parsed only through `parseNoteYaml` (`services/noteYaml.ts`), which checks the text against `NOTE_YAML_LIMITS` first (32 KB of text among them); a lint rule keeps `parseYaml` out of every other file. `tests/unit/noteYaml.test.ts` compares its count with the YAML library over a small fixed sample of texts; `VITE_NOTE_YAML_TRIALS=600000` runs more.
- `creatureValues.ts` normalises values for every system: ratings (`"1/4"`, `½`, `"Creature 3"`, `"3+1*"`, `−1`) and options (links, Fantasy Statblocks' encoded links and page references stripped, compared case-insensitively). `creatureFilterEngine.ts` is pure: options within a filter are OR (or all required, `match: 'all'`), filters AND, each facet counts as if its own filter were off, and a token lacking a required option's data is hidden and counted in `hidden`. Option filters and the layout facet hold `OptionPicks` (`include` / `exclude`); an excluded value hides every token that has it and keeps those without the field. Edit picks only through `creatureSelection.ts` (`toggleOption` for a click, `toggleExcludedOption` for a double or Alt-click, `withOptionState`). The alignment filter reads parts, not phrases (`alignmentParts`: Lawful, Neutral, Chaotic, Good, Evil, Unaligned, Any; `CE` and `L` abbreviations too) and requires every picked part.
- The filters live in the search, as in Valkenhall's deck builder: typed `keyword:value` tokens (`type:beast`, `cr>=5`, `cr:1/4-3`, `tag:forest`, `statblock:no`, quotes for spaces; `-type:beast` or `type!=beast` exclude where the keyword is `negatable`) with autocomplete for keywords and for the values in view, the filter panel behind the button at the end of the field (`AdvancedFilterPanel`; the button is on every tab and disabled where a tab has no panel yet, so the header never shifts between tabs), and a chip per active filter above the content (`ActiveFilterBar`). The syntax is generic (`src/app/search/querySyntax.ts`); the asset manager's keywords, suggestions and token application live in `asset-manager/search/`. The filters' options and counts come from the open folder and every folder below it (`useCreatureFilters`), what an active filter searches, so a root holding only folders still offers its subfolders' statblocks. Committed tokens leave the text and become filters; the name search uses only the plain words (`useSearchKeywords`), so a half-typed token never empties the list. Tab and Escape in the field stop propagating while the suggestions use them, since the asset manager's shortcuts listen on the document. Cmd+F (Ctrl+F off macOS) is an Obsidian key scope pushed while the search is mounted (`useSearchShortcut`): Obsidian binds Mod+F to "Search current file" and consumes it before any DOM listener. Option values drop private-use characters (rulebook-font glyphs), and the Type filter reads categories without a bracketed detail (`parseCategories`: "Horde (10/HP)" is Horde).
- The Rating sort orders characters by the first of `RATING_FILTERS` their statblock has, grouped by scale, with unrated characters last in either order.
